message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different kinds of workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – originally for drawing images, now also used for massively parallel compute tasks. |
| **Core count** | Few cores (typically 2–32 on consumer devices). | Hundreds or thousands of smaller cores. |
| **Core design** | Complex, high‑performance cores with deep pipelines, branch prediction, large caches, and sophisticated control logic. | Simple, lightweight cores optimized for throughput; each core does less work individually but many can run simultaneously. |
| **Instruction set** | Rich, complex instruction sets (x86, ARM) with support for branching, exceptions, and varied data types. | Simpler, SIMD‑style instructions that operate on vectors of data; fewer branches. |
| **Memory hierarchy** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches per core, fast access to main memory. | Smaller per‑core caches; relies heavily on high‑bandwidth memory (GDDR, HBM). |
| **Latency vs throughput** | Optimized for low latency – quick response to individual requests. | Optimized for high throughput – many operations performed in parallel, tolerating higher latency. |
| **Typical workloads** | Single‑threaded or lightly parallel tasks, system management, database queries, web servers. | Highly parallel tasks: rendering frames, scientific simulations, machine learning inference/training, cryptocurrency mining. |
| **Programming model** | Traditional sequential programming (C/C++, Java, etc.). | Parallel programming models (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan compute, DirectCompute). |

In short, a CPU excels at handling diverse, irregular tasks quickly, while a GPU shines when you can break a problem into many identical, independent operations that can be executed concurrently. This makes GPUs ideal for graphics, deep learning, and other data‑parallel workloads, whereas CPUs remain essential for general-purpose computing.
